source.title: Sleep deprivation disrupts the gatekeeping role of confidence in belief updating

confidence_rationale: Two preregistered within-subject studies (N=36, N=49) with a clean and specific result: 24-hour total sleep deprivation did not merely make people worse, it removed the normal protective effect of high confidence on belief revision. That is a precision-weighting failure, which is the closest empirical handle in this pull on MECH-017's 'uncertainty recalibration'. Confidence is nonetheless the lowest of the empirical entries because the mapping is inferential: social belief updating is not world-model uncertainty, and a deprivation deficit shows sleep is necessary for maintenance without showing that sleep performs recalibration.
failure_signatures: The design is deprivation-versus-rested, so it cannot separate 'sleep recalibrates uncertainty' from 'wakefulness degrades it and sleep merely halts the degradation' -- only the first of these is MECH-017.

Sleep deprivation increased belief change regardless of feedback type, which is consistent with a general loss of response inhibition or effortful control rather than a specific miscalibration of uncertainty.
Only 24-hour total deprivation was tested; if partial sleep restriction leaves confidence-gating intact, the graded dose-response that a recalibration mechanism predicts would be absent.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In two preregistered within-subject studies, 24 hours of total sleep deprivation increased belief change irrespective of feedback type and disrupted the stabilising role of initial confidence: high-confidence beliefs, normally resistant to revision, were revised more often when participants were sleep deprived, and larger confidence drops predicted more frequent belief change.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-017 lists uncertainty recalibration as one of three operations but the architecture doc says nothing about what a failure of it would look like. This paper supplies the signature: not uniformly higher or lower confidence, but a broken coupling between confidence and update magnitude -- beliefs held precisely stop behaving as though they were. In REE terms that is a precision-weighting failure on the posterior, and it gives the claim a dependent variable an experiment could actually measure, which 'recalibration' alone does not.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The beliefs here are social and propositional, revised under peer feedback; MECH-017 is about the generative model of a physical world. Treating the two as the same quantity is the main transfer risk, and it is a real one -- confidence in a stated opinion may be regulated by mechanisms quite separate from precision on a sensory prediction. The deprivation design also licenses only the necessity direction: sleep is needed for calibrated gating to survive, which is weaker than the claim that sleep is when recalibration is performed.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adult humans; 24 h total sleep deprivation vs rested; belief-updating task with peer feedback; two preregistered within-subject studies (N=36, N=49).

confidence_components.notes: source_quality is high on method grounds -- preregistered, replicated across two samples, within-subject. mapping_fidelity is the constraint and is set deliberately low: this is the only entry where the REE translation requires an inference across domains (social belief -> world-model precision) rather than a change of vocabulary.
